The timings are sequential single samples and cannot establish intrinsic speed superiority. Both generic helpers still report [propext, Quot.sound]. Elimination required_type and both real-number targets report all three. The installed collector traverses theorem/definition types and values, supporting the diagnostic conclusion that changing only the proof body does not remove dependencies already observed in that elaborated type under the pinned environment. This is not a general impossibility theorem.

The final checker replayed the strongest successful source from each. These results establish a bounded negative outcome under the fixed gate; no baseline comparison is made here.

Independent adaptive final checker, actor agent/a644348c-2037-4557-b445-c9df0896a2a0. Exactly TWO Lean invocations total, one byte-for-byte replay per Round 2 finding, using the supplied Python guard with --seconds 300 --memory-mib 8192. No other Lean command or build. Independence means a separate actor and actual replay, not a different model or independent initial derivation. Only the two assigned Round 2 findings and their cited Round 1 provenance were inspected.

Environment two-round-lean-v1; pinned Lean 4.35.0 (leanprover/lean4:v4.35.0); context c33461ada7554b5d422bfb549ea40e0c83355f115d1de52bd75f2e1227908c7e; checker 6e9fafb9cd397abaa610c3676e27f404ef63926486c131734fdaebe9fd1c1b40. The HTTPS artifact is tracked protocol/context provenance at a pinned repository revision, not hosted replay evidence. Complete sources, logs and receipts are preserved in the shared local worker directory and included below. Taskvalet records the report but did not execute or certify the proof. The 50ms sampled process-tree RSS watchdog is not a kernel hard memory ceiling; single-run timings are not comparative performance evidence. Bundled 0.14.0 skills were exported to this worker's local directory and all three checked current; no global skills changed. No lemma export is admissible under the unchanged empty-axiom gate. No acceptance is requested.
